To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 4 Mb SEU cross section is correlated with the SEPCM lineal energy deposition spectra.

the lineal energy spectrum of a silicon proportional counter microdosimetric detector changes with the hardness of an incident neutron spectrum and this change correlates to the single event upset cross section for an SRAM memory device.
the SEPCM is a useful dosimeter in neutron environments and the SEU cross section of the 4Mb SRAM is a function of both the incident neutron energy and the lineal energy deposition spectrum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing the feasibility of a new method of neutron dosimetric measurement using silicon equivalent proportional counter detectors (SEPCMs).
the development of a silicon equivalent proportional microdosimeter for use in the measurement of neutron radiation environments.
the correlation of the lineal energy spectrum and single event upset (seu) cross sections for silicon microelectronics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the correlation of the lineal energy response of the SEPCM with the SEU cross section for 4 Mb SRAMS was good for all incident neutron energy spectra.
the SEU cross sections of the SRAM were not a direct function of the SEPCM measured lineal energy spectra.
the SEU cross section for the 4 Mb RAM is a function of the neutron energy spectra and that the SEPCM is a suitable neutron dosimeter to correlate with SEU cross sections.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
as the incident neutron energy spectrum becomes harder (i.e., higher average neutron energy) the lineal energy response becomes harder, and the SEU cross section increases.
a silicon equivalent microdosimeter and SEU cross sections can be correlated.
the 4 Mb SEU cross section is correlated to a neutron energy spectrum weighted average lineal energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a SEPCM is a viable dosimeter for characterizing neutron energy spectra for space radiation effects testing.
SEU cross sections can be predicted from the SEPCM response to the incident neutron energy spectrum.
the SEPCM can be used as a neutron dosimeter and that the lineal energy spectrum response from the SEPCMs can be used to estimate SEU cross sections from neutron exposure.
